title: Hostinger Reach, Mailchimp or Brevo: which to choose for email marketing
seoTitle: Is Hostinger Reach worth it? Comparison with Mailchimp and Brevo
description: Reach is worth it if you already have a Hostinger site and a list of up to 1,000 recipients; bigger lists fit Mailchimp or Brevo better. See how it compares with their free plans.
metaDescription: Is Hostinger Reach worth it? Chart by profile, plans, sending limits, WhatsApp and renewal in US dollars on October 30, 2026, compared with the free plans of Mailchimp and Brevo.
imageAlt: Hostinger logo with email and chart icons, and the word Reach on the band

contentSections.heading: Quick answer
paragraphs: Reach is worth it for anyone who already has a site on Hostinger and a list of up to 1,000 recipients. Anyone starting with no budget can use the free plan of Mailchimp or Brevo first. The sending limit and WhatsApp decide; SONAR20 gives 20% on the first period of a new purchase.

contentSections.heading: Which one for whom: the chart
paragraphs: The right question is not which tool is best, but how many people are on your list, how many emails you send a month and whether you need WhatsApp. The chart sums up the choice by what the pricing pages of Hostinger, Mailchimp and Brevo said:

rows: Small list, starting with no budget
Brevo's free plan sends up to 300 emails a day, with no card. Mailchimp is free below 250 contacts. The three Reach plans are paid.
Has a Hostinger site and a list of up to 500
US$ 1.74 a month in the first 12 months (renews at US$ 2.49), 3,500 emails a month, no Reach branding and with automations.
WhatsApp is only in Pro, at US$ 2.79 a month in the first 12 months (renews at US$ 3.99). The page does not show the cost per message. On Brevo, WhatsApp is in the Professional plan.
Past the free limit, up to 1,000 contacts
Grow covers up to 500 recipients. Pro goes up to 1,000 recipients for US$ 2.79 a month in the first 12 months (renews at US$ 3.99).
The Reach plans stop at 1,000 recipients and 7,000 emails a month.

postParagraphs: If your list fits in the free plan of Mailchimp or Brevo, start there and pay when you pass the limit. If you already have a Hostinger site and the list is past a few hundred, Reach is the one to compare first.

contentSections.heading: The Reach plans
paragraphs: Three paid plans, no free one: Starter, Grow and Pro. At checkout, Grow shows up as “Reach 500”, for its limit of 500 recipients. The prices below are from Hostinger's global page, in US dollars, read on October 30, 2026, during the Black Friday campaign. They can vary by country and currency, and they can change:
The page gives 30 days to ask for a refund.
postParagraphs: The renewal is what matters: on Grow and Pro it goes up compared with the campaign price. The plans, from the page:
bullets: **Starter:** 100 recipients, 200 emails a month and no AI credits. The emails carry the Reach branding.
**Grow:** 500 recipients, 3,500 emails a month and 10 AI credits a month. It removes the Reach branding and adds personalization, scheduling and automations.
**Pro:** 1,000 recipients, 7,000 emails a month and 20 AI credits a month. It adds HTML, optimized send time, WhatsApp campaigns, custom fields and team members.
contentSections.emphasis: When you are torn between the plans, the size of your list decides. The plans on the page go up to 1,000 recipients; above that, check at checkout whether a larger Pro tier exists, or go with Mailchimp or Brevo.

contentSections.heading: Mailchimp and Brevo: the free plans
paragraphs: Both have a free plan, and Reach does not. The Mailchimp and Brevo pages were read on October 30, 2026; their paid prices are left out of this comparison, because they were not read in US dollars:

rows: For fewer than 250 contacts. When the list goes past the limit, sending pauses.
Forever, with no card needed and up to 300 emails a day.

postParagraphs: What Mailchimp and Brevo offer that Reach does not is a free plan to start with and larger contact tiers, for when the list grows.

contentSections.heading: WhatsApp: only in Reach Pro
paragraphs: On the Reach page, WhatsApp marketing campaigns appear only in Pro, at US$ 2.79 a month in the first 12 months (renews at US$ 3.99 a month). Starter and Grow don't have them. The page does not show how much each WhatsApp message costs, so check the dashboard before you count on this channel.
On Brevo, WhatsApp appears among the channels of the Professional plan. For anyone who needs WhatsApp with a list of up to 1,000 contacts, Reach Pro is the plan to look at.

contentSections.heading: When the list grows
paragraphs: The first limit that matters is the number of recipients: 100 on Starter, 500 on Grow and 1,000 on Pro. The Reach plans on the page stop there. The limit counts unique recipients in the month, not stored contacts. Anyone who has or expects more than 1,000 contacts should go to Mailchimp or Brevo, which charge by contact range or by sending volume.

The second limit is sending volume. On Grow, 3,500 emails a month with 500 recipients add up to 7 sends to the whole list in a month; on Pro, 7,000 emails with 1,000 recipients also make 7. The cap is monthly and counts every email sent, so multiply your month's sends by the real number of recipients. A weekly newsletter fits.
bullets: **Still without a domain?** If you want your site's address on the sender, see [Hostinger domain: buy it there, transfer it or register elsewhere](/en/reviews/hostinger-domain-buy-transfer-or-elsewhere).
**Going to change tools later?** Export your contact list before cancelling the old plan, and check how the new tool imports it.

contentSections.heading: SONAR20 and the price of Reach
paragraphs: Use the code **SONAR20** in the cart's coupon field, or come in through this article's link: it is **20% off the first period**. Bruno tested it on Reach 500 for 24 months, and the discount applied in the cart.

The price on the page and the price in the cart can differ on the same day, so check the cart to see which price applies to you and how much SONAR20 takes off it. For the other Reach plans and periods, it was not tested; check the cart. The full rule for the code is in [Hostinger coupons](/en/coupons/hostinger).

contentSections.heading: Is it worth it? The verdict
paragraphs: **Worth it** for anyone who already has a Hostinger site and a list of up to 1,000 recipients. Grow covers a list of up to 500 with automations; Pro covers a list of up to 1,000 and WhatsApp. The renewal of Grow (US$ 2.49 a month) and of Pro (US$ 3.99 a month) is part of the decision, so check it before you pay.
**Stay on the free Mailchimp or Brevo plan** if your list is just starting and you don't yet know whether you will send email often. Reach has no free plan.
**Go with Mailchimp or Brevo** if your list passes 1,000 contacts or if your monthly emails, automations included, pass 7,000, the Pro ceiling. The Reach plans stop at 1,000 recipients.
If it were for my site, I would take Reach Grow, because it covers a list of up to 500 with automations and renews at US$ 2.49 a month.

contentSections.heading: Frequently asked questions
bullets: Is Hostinger Reach worth it? It is, for anyone with a Hostinger site and a list of up to 1,000 recipients. Grow costs US$ 1.74 a month in the first 12 months and renews at US$ 2.49 a month.

How much does Hostinger Reach cost? On Hostinger's global page, in US dollars: Starter US$ 1.49, Grow US$ 1.74 and Pro US$ 2.79 a month in the first 12 months, renewing at US$ 1.49, US$ 2.49 and US$ 3.99. Prices can vary by country and currency.
Does Hostinger Reach have a free plan? No: its three plans are paid. Mailchimp is free for fewer than 250 contacts, and Brevo has a free plan with up to 300 emails a day.
Does Hostinger Reach have WhatsApp? Yes, only in the Pro plan. The page does not show the cost per message; check the dashboard.
What is Reach 500? It is the name Grow takes in the Hostinger cart, after its limit of 500 recipients. It sends 3,500 emails a month.
Hostinger Reach or Mailchimp? For a list of up to 1,000 recipients and a Hostinger site, Reach. To start for free, or for a list above 1,000 contacts, Mailchimp or Brevo.
Does the SONAR20 code work on Hostinger Reach? Yes: in Bruno's test, the discount applied to Reach 500 for 24 months. For the other plans and periods it was not tested; check the cart.
Can existing Hostinger customers use SONAR20? It applies to an eligible new purchase, even with an existing account. Domain registration and renewal are excluded.

takeIf: Take Reach if you already have a Hostinger site and your list fits within 1,000 recipients.
Take Reach Pro if you need to send messages on WhatsApp.
Take it if both the unique recipients in a month and the total of campaign and automation emails fit the plan's limits.
skipIf: Skip it if your list is just starting and fits in the free plan of Mailchimp or Brevo.
Skip it if the unique recipients or the total of monthly emails exceed the plan's limits.
